title: PopPy: Opportunistically Exploiting Parallelism in Python Compound AI Applications
description: Research paper on a system that exploits parallelism in compound AI applications written as sequential Python code. PopPy addresses three key challenges: Python's language complexity, dynamic dispatch obscuring parallelization opportunities, and minimal developer effort requirements.
author: ArXiv Research

title: The last six months in LLMs in five minutes
description: A lightning talk at PyCon US 2026 with annotated slides covering recent developments in LLMs, including new models, tools, and capabilities.
author: Simon Willison

title: Gemini 3.5 Flash: more expensive, but Google plan to use it for everything
description: Analysis of Google's new Gemini 3.5 Flash model released at Google I/O, which Google is using extensively across their products. Discusses pricing implications and Google's strategy. Also covers upcoming Gemini Spark agent and Antigravity CLI tool transitions.
author: Simon Willison

title: SpecBench: Measuring Reward Hacking in Long-Horizon Coding Agents
description: A benchmark for measuring reward hacking in long-horizon coding agents. Addresses the challenge of evaluating AI agents that may game reward signals rather than genuinely solving problems.
author: Bingchen Zhao, Dhruv Srikanth, Yuxiang Wu, Zhengyao Jiang

title: Agent JIT Compilation for Latency-Optimizing Web Agent Planning and Scheduling
description: Research on just-in-time compilation for AI agents to optimize latency in web agent planning and scheduling. Accepted at ICML 2026.
author: Caleb Winston, Ron Yifeng Wang, Azalia Mirhoseini, Christos Kozyrakis

title: Insights Generator: Systematic Corpus-Level Trace Diagnostics for LLM Agents
description: A system for generating systematic corpus-level trace diagnostics for LLM agents, helping understand and debug agent behavior at scale.
author: Akshay Manglik, Apaar Shanker, Kaustubh Deshpande, et al.

title: AutoRPA: Efficient GUI Automation through LLM-Driven Code Synthesis from Interactions
description: Research on automating GUI interactions through LLM-driven code synthesis. Accepted in ICML 2026, demonstrating how AI can learn from user interactions to automate repetitive tasks.
author: Minghao Chen, Xinyi Hu, Zhou Yu, Yufei Yin

title: GDS weighs in on the NHS's decision to retreat from Open Source
description: Coverage of UK Government Digital Service's response to NHS closing open source repositories. GDS recommends keeping open by default, warning that making everything private adds costs and reduces reuse and scrutiny. Discusses AI, open code, and vulnerability risk in the public sector.
author: Simon Willison

title: OpenClaw's name history traced through Git
description: Fascinating trace of OpenClaw's name evolution through Git history: Warelay → CLAWDIS → CLAWDBOT → Clawdbot → Moltbot → OpenClaw, showing the project's journey from WhatsApp relay to personal AI assistant.
author: Simon Willison

title: QR code generator built with Claude assistance
description: Built a QR code generator tool for URLs/text and WiFi networks with help from Claude. The tool includes options for network name, password, security type, styling, size, and color.
author: Simon Willison

title: Datasette-llm-limits: Per-user spending limits for LLM usage
description: Released a plugin for Datasette that configures per-user or global spending limits for LLM usage, helping control costs. Example shows $1/day per user limit with 24-hour rolling window.
author: Simon Willison

title: Coding agents make programming languages increasingly fungible
description: Discussion of how coding agents have changed the lock-in dynamics of programming languages. Cites example of company using AI to rewrite apps to React Native, and Mitchell Hashimoto's observation about Bun migrating from Zig to Rust. Programming languages used to be LOCK IN, and they're increasingly not so.
author: Simon Willison

title: Rate limiting plugin built with Codex (GPT-5.5 xhigh)
description: Used OpenAI Codex desktop (GPT-5.5 xhigh) to build a configurable rate limiting plugin for Datasette to block poorly-behaved crawlers. Includes production configuration example with IP-based blocking and path-specific rules.
author: Simon Willison

title: Andrej Karpathy on the 'Slopacolypse' and AI's dramatic impact on programming
description: At Sequoia AI Ascent 2026, Karpathy discussed bracing for 2026 as the 'year of the slopacolypse,' noting how dramatically programming has changed in the last two months. While he coined 'vibe coding' last year, he now says he's 'never felt more behind as a programmer.' He also called Claude Code 'the first convincing demonstration of what an LLM Agent looks like' and 'AI that lives on your computer.'
author: Andrej Karpathy

title: Karpathy: AI is suddenly writing most of my code
description: According to Reddit discussions, Karpathy mentioned that 'AI is suddenly writing most of his code' and he is 'starting to atrophy' his ability to write code himself, highlighting the rapid shift in software development practices.
author: Andrej Karpathy

title: DeepWeb-Bench: A Deep Research Benchmark Demanding Massive Cross-Source Evidence and Long-Horizon Derivation
description: A new benchmark for evaluating AI systems on deep research tasks that require aggregating evidence from multiple sources and performing long-horizon reasoning. Work in Progress with 27 pages, 10 figures, and 4 tables.
author: Sixiong Xie, Zhuofan Shi, Haiyang Shen, et al.

title: PALS: Power-Aware LLM Serving for Mixture-of-Experts Models
description: Research on power-aware LLM serving systems specifically designed for mixture-of-experts models, addressing energy efficiency in AI deployment.
author: Can Hankendi, Rana Shahout, Minlan Yu, Ayse K. Coskun

title: AgentAtlas: Beyond Outcome Leaderboards for LLM Agents
description: A framework for evaluating LLM agents that goes beyond simple outcome-based leaderboards to provide more nuanced assessment of agent capabilities.
author: Parsa Mazaheri, Kasra Mazaheri

title: Open-World Evaluations for Measuring Frontier AI Capabilities
description: A comprehensive framework for open-world evaluations to measure frontier AI capabilities, addressing the limitations of closed benchmarks. Authored by researchers from multiple institutions including Sayash Kapoor, Peter Kirgis, and Andrew Schwartz.
author: Sayash Kapoor, Peter Kirgis, Andrew Schwartz, et al.

title: Quality and Security Signals in AI-Generated Python Refactoring Pull Requests
description: Study examining quality and security signals in AI-generated Python refactoring pull requests, providing insights into the safety and reliability of AI-assisted code refactoring.
author: Mohamed Almukhtar, Anwar Ghammam, Hua Ming

title: Stdlib or Third-Party? Empirical Performance and Correctness of LLM-Assisted Zero-Dependency Python Libraries
description: Empirical study comparing performance and correctness of using standard library vs third-party packages in LLM-assisted zero-dependency Python libraries.
author: Peng Ding, Rick Stevens

title: Governance by Construction for Generalist Agents
description: Research on 'governance by construction' approaches for generalist AI agents, focusing on building safety and governance into the fundamental architecture of AI systems.
author: Segev Shlomov, Iftach Shoham, Alon Oved, et al.

title: PlanningBench: Generating Scalable and Verifiable Planning Data for Evaluating and Training Large Language Models
description: A benchmark for generating scalable and verifiable planning data to evaluate and train LLMs on planning tasks, addressing the challenge of assessing reasoning capabilities.
author: Ziliang Zhao, Zenan Xu, Shuting Wang, et al.

title: Evaluating Temporal Semantic Caching and Workflow Optimization in Agentic Plan-Execute Pipelines
description: Research on evaluating temporal semantic caching and workflow optimization techniques in agentic plan-execute pipelines, with 13 pages and 8 figures.
author: Alimurtaza Mustafa Merchant, Krish Veera, Sajal Kumar Goyla, et al.

title: COAgents: Multi-Agent Framework to Learn and Navigate Routing Problems Search Space
description: A multi-agent framework for learning and navigating routing problems search space. Accepted at LION 2026, The Learning and Intelligent Optimization Conference.
author: Oleksandr Yakovenko, Mahdi Mostajabdaveh, Cheikh Ahmed, et al.

title: From Automated to Autonomous: Hierarchical Agent-native Network Architecture (HANA)
description: Research on hierarchical agent-native network architecture (HANA) for transitioning from automated to autonomous systems. Accepted by IEEE Networking Letters.
author: Binghan Wu, Shoufeng Wang, Yunxin Liu, et al.

title: SOLAR: A Self-Optimizing Open-Ended Autonomous Agent for Lifelong Learning and Continual Adaptation
description: A self-optimizing open-ended autonomous agent designed for lifelong learning and continual adaptation. Accepted at AAAI 2026 Conference in Streaming Continual Learning Bridge.
author: Nitin Vetcha, Dianbo Liu

title: AgentCo-op: Retrieval-Based Synthesis of Interoperable Multi-Agent Workflows
description: Research on retrieval-based synthesis of interoperable multi-agent workflows, enabling agents to work together more effectively.
author: Shuaike Shen, Wenduo Cheng, Shike Wang, et al.

title: Personality Engineering with AI Agents: A New Methodology for Negotiation Research
description: A new methodology for negotiation research using AI agents with engineered personalities, exploring how different personality traits affect negotiation outcomes.
author: Michelle A. Vaccaro, Jared R. Curhan

title: Tool-Augmented Agent for Closed-loop Optimization, Simulation, and Modeling Orchestration
description: Research on tool-augmented agents for closed-loop optimization, simulation, and modeling orchestration, enabling AI to manage complex scientific workflows.
author: Liyuan Deng, Shujian Deng, Yongkang Chen, et al.

title: Declarative Data Services: Structured Agentic Discovery for Composing Data Systems
description: Research on declarative data services using structured agentic discovery for composing data systems, enabling more intelligent data system design.
author: Shanshan Ye, Duo Lu

title: AiraXiv: An AI-Driven Open-Access Platform for Human and AI Scientists
description: An AI-driven open-access platform designed to serve both human and AI scientists, representing a new approach to scientific publishing and discovery.
author: Junshu Pan, Panzhong Lu, Yixuan Weng, et al.
